criteria: `truncate(value, width)` in `text.py` returns a result that is never longer than `width` characters.
`truncate(value, width)` returns a value of `width` characters or fewer unchanged, including a value of exactly `width` characters: `truncate("abcdefghij", 10)` is `"abcdefghij"`.

`truncate(value, width)` cuts a value longer than `width` to its first `width - 3` characters and adds `"..."`, so the dots are counted in the width: `truncate("abcdefghijklmnop", 10)` is `"abcdefg..."`.

`truncate(value, width)` does not leave whitespace in front of the dots: when the kept part ends in whitespace, that whitespace is removed before the dots are added, and the result is then shorter than `width`: `truncate("hello world again", 9)` is `"hello..."`.
`truncate(value, width)` does not trim a value that fits: `truncate("  hi  ", 10)` is `"  hi  "`.
`truncate(value, width)` raises `ValueError` when `width` is below 4, and this is checked first, so it also holds for a value that would fit: `truncate("ab", 3)` raises `ValueError`.
`truncate(value, width)` raises `TypeError` when `value` is not a `str`.
